document.about: opendataloader-bench 01030000000007: one page of a book of Chuj narratives, set in a Garamond whose embedded CFF program has its own encoding and no ToUnicode map. It names its small capitals, old-style figures and ligatures by variant and ligature names (`h.sc`, `one.osf`, `f_i`).

notes: 2026-11-26: the interpreter reads a glyph's text from a name only where the Adobe Glyph List lists the whole name, so every small capital, old-style figure and ligature read as nothing: `T narratives told in Chuj`, `eld work on Chuj from to .`, `[CAC R]`. The program's names are now read by the list's own rules: a variant after a period, a ligature's glyphs between underscores, `uniXXXX` sequences.

checks.issue: The small capitals after the drop cap read as nothing: `T narratives told in Chuj`.
checks.text: This collection of six narratives told in Chuj

checks.issue: The old-style years and the fi ligature read as nothing: `during eld work on Chuj from to .`
checks.text: recorded by me during field work on Chuj from 1964 to 1965.

checks.issue: The archive codes' old-style figures read as nothing: `[CAC R]`.
checks.text: An Old Man Whose Son Killed Him [CAC 002 R022]

checks.issue: The running head in small capitals was lost.
